acceptance_thresholds_are_not_set: Every `minimum` below is null on purpose. Tracker row R11-FP13 records acceptance thresholds as the domain owner's decision, to be made before the answer-correctness run, and `scripts/answer_evaluation_benchmark.py` supplies no default: a metric with a null minimum reports `no threshold set` and cannot pass or fail. Filling in a minimum and the `sign_off` block below is all that is required to make the gate enforce it -- no code change. Do not copy a measurement out of `metrics` into a `minimum`: a measurement is what happened, a threshold is what is acceptable, and conflating them makes the benchmark grade itself.

proposed_thresholds.how_to_adopt: Copy a `proposed_minimum` into the matching `thresholds.<name>.minimum`, then fill `sign_off.signed_off_by` and `sign_off.signed_off_at`. No code change is needed. Adopt them one at a time if you prefer -- a null minimum and a set one coexist fine.
proposed_thresholds.not_proposed_and_why: answer_table_pass_rate, answer_text_pass_rate and result_set_match_rate measured null -- meaning not measured, not zero. They need the live paid run. overall_case_pass_rate folds them in, so it is left alone too: proposing a number for a metric nothing has measured is exactly the failure this file warns about.

answer_verdict_pass_rate.rationale: This metric folds both directions, and they are not symmetric: refusing something answerable is an annoyance, while answering something that should have been refused is a governance breach. Since one direction has no acceptable failure rate, the combined metric takes the stricter bar, and the corpus grows rather than the bar dropping.

evidence_support_rate.rationale: The one genuinely probabilistic metric here: it measures retrieval, which the repository already treats as tolerance-bearing -- scripts/quality_benchmark.py gates its retrieval metrics at 5 points of drift rather than demanding an exact figure, for the reason R11-FP09 records, that an exact bar turns into a test of whether a provider was configured. 0.90 leaves room for one miss in ten while still failing a systematic regression.

refusal_reason_code_pass_rate.rationale: No tolerance, because this is a safety control rather than a quality metric. The file's own note says a refusal for the wrong reason is not a correct refusal; a partial credit here would mean accepting that the platform sometimes declines for a reason it made up.

unapproved_evidence_avoidance_rate.rationale: Standing on unapproved evidence is a governance failure, not a quality shortfall -- the whole point of the governed context product is that an answer stands only on what was approved. One case is thin cover for a 1.0 bar, so treat this as the metric most in need of more cases.

proposed_thresholds.proposed_by: review-2026-09-16 follow-up cycle, at the user's request
proposed_thresholds.status: PROPOSED -- not signed off, and not enforced. Every `minimum` in `thresholds` is still null.
proposed_thresholds.the_honest_caveat: These are reasoned from what the offline mode measured, NOT copied from it -- the file's own warning against copying a measurement into a threshold is right. But the case counts are 1 to 5. A 1.0 over three cases is weak evidence for demanding 1.0 of a larger corpus, so the real limiter here is corpus size, not the numbers below. Growing the corpus should come before tightening any of them.

sign_off.note: Who set the thresholds below, and when. Left null until the domain owner (tracker row R11-FP13: AI quality lead) signs them off.

answer_table_pass_rate.note: Share of cases whose generated SQL referenced every table the case requires and none it forbids. Needs the live run; the no-provider mode cannot measure it.

answer_text_pass_rate.note: Share of cases whose explanation contains what the case requires and excludes what it forbids. Needs the live run.

answer_verdict_pass_rate.note: Share of cases that were answered when they should be answered and refused when they should be refused. A refusal is an expected verdict here, not an outcome bucket.

evidence_support_rate.note: Share of cases whose retrieved context contained every enriched-footprint object the answer is expected to stand on. Measured without a provider.

overall_case_pass_rate.note: Share of cases where every sub-score that could be measured passed. Cases where nothing could be measured are excluded from the denominator rather than counted as passes.

refusal_reason_code_pass_rate.note: Share of refused cases that refused with the reason code the case names. A refusal for the wrong reason is not a correct refusal.

result_set_match_rate.note: Share of cases carrying gold_sql whose answer returned an equivalent result set. Needs the live run against an estate holding real rows.

unapproved_evidence_avoidance_rate.note: Share of gap cases where the answer did not reach an object whose only path is lineage nobody approved. The answer-level counterpart of the retrieval half's gap preservation.

token_basis: Tokens only; no dollar amount. `provider_reported_tokens` is what the provider said it billed for the attempt that answered (ProviderUsage, via the run's plan_evidence.model_call_evidence). `estimated_tokens` is the gateway's 4-bytes-per-token heuristic across the attempt chain, which is the figure the agent contract's caps were checked against before the call. `charged_tokens` and `basis` come from agent_orchestrator.run_token_charge, the same function that reconciles AgentBudgetWindow, so this report and the budget window cannot disagree. The two kinds are not interchangeable and are never summed together into one number. No dollar cost is derived: per cost_showback.py this platform has no billing integration and no reconciled spend figure, and a price-list multiplication would be an invention, not a measurement.
